newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees growth in sugar output, exports.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees growth in sugar output, exports.

text.p: Australia's sugar state of Queensland had the potential to produce 6.5 million tonnes of raw sugar by the year 2003, up from the 5.156 million tonnes of 1996, Harry Bonanno, chairman of CANEGROWERS, said on Wednesday.
Production increases would depend on whether prices remained attractive to producers, he told the 1997 Australian Sugar Convention.
But the industry had to address how to handle larger crops within a standard season length, he said.

Delivering the opening address to the conference, Bonanno said that since 1970 the volume of cane crushed each year had more than doubled, even though the number of factories had declined to 25 from 31.
Bonanno also said the proportion of Queensland's exported sugar production was expected to increase to about 90 percent by 2000 from about 86 percent at present.
The Queensland sugar industry had become one of the world's largest sugar exporters, together with Brazil, Thailand and the European Union, he said.
"It now accounts for about 16 percent of world (sugar) trade and is consistently the world's largest exporter of raw sugar," Bonanno said.
With more than A$1.7 billion sold to export markets, sugar had outpaced cattle as Queensland's main rural earner and was second as a whole only to coal.
In 1996 Queensland Sugar Corp was Australia's eighth largest exporter, surpassed by only one other agricultural body, the Australian Wheat Board, he said.
Australia was disadvantaged against competitors which had lower labour costs and/or government assistance but it had a well-organised industry and efficient cane production, Bonanno said.
